# The Anchorage Address

> An Alaska Native-owned firm just won a $24.96M Navy contract for autonomous stealth boats. They will be built in Oregon.

Published 2026-07-14 by Alaska AI. 8 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-14/

## The story

The boat is Alaskan. The shipyard is not.

An Anchorage, Native-owned firm won a $24.96M Navy contract for autonomous stealth vessels. They will be built in Oregon.

The Navy did not shop around.

AMOUNT $24,960,408 · FOR autonomous low-profile vessels · TO ReconCraft LLC, Anchorage, Alaska · BUILT IN Clackamas, Oregon · DONE BY November 2028 · BOUGHT sole source, no competition · PAID FROM FY2026 innovative technologies (Navy)

Built to show almost nothing.

FREEBOARD under 0.61 m · LENGTH about 19.75 m (65 ft) · PAYLOAD 2,000 to 4,627 kg · RANGE about 2,200 nautical miles. The hull is borrowed from narco-submarines, tuned to beat radar, sonar, sight and heat.

No crew. Not yet a mind.

What the Navy wants next, run itself in crowded ports, with GPS jammed and comms down. What it does today, no one aboard, driven by remote control and pre-set waypoints. Autonomous is the plan, not yet the whole reality.

A set-aside did the winning.

The Navy bought this sole source under the SBA 8(a) program, the federal channel that routes contracts to Native-owned and disadvantaged small firms. Native-owned, tribally owned, 8(a) certified through Dec 2, 2026. The program is doing what it was built to do.

Owned up here. Welded down there.

ANCHORAGE, ALASKA, incorporated here, Native-owned, the address on the contract. CLACKAMAS, OREGON, the shipyard, where the steel is actually cut, hulls up to 120 ft. Two states, one boat, one flag on the contract.

Alaska's seat in the robot-boat boom is an ownership stake, not a shipyard.

That is a real Alaska Native business win. It is also most of what Alaska's slice looks like right now.

An Alaska industry, or just an Alaska address?

If a Native-owned firm wins the contract but the boats are built Outside, does the win count as Alaska's? Tell me where you land. Sources in the comments.

## What we verified

- Naval Sea Systems Command awarded ReconCraft LLC, Anchorage, Alaska, a $24,960,408 firm-fixed-price contract for autonomous low-profile vessels. [U.S. Department of War (DoD) daily contracts](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report, 2026-07-08.
- Current ALPVs operate with no onboard personnel using remote control and waypoint navigation, with provisions for enhanced autonomous capability in the future; the Defense Innovation Unit wants them to navigate autonomously in congested waters and when communications and GPS are denied. [Army Recognition](https://armyrecognition.com/news/navy-news/2025/us-marines-train-in-japan-with-alpv-autonomous-low-profile-vessel-based-on-narco-submarine-designs-for-stealth-operations), report, 2025-04-24.
- ReconCraft has a track record of Navy special-operations and patrol craft, including a 2023 contract worth about $35.9 million for a dozen 40-foot patrol boats and a role in a combined $290 million patrol-boat award alongside Louisiana-based Metal Shark for the Navy's Naval Expeditionary Combat Command. [Shephard Media](https://www.shephardmedia.com/news/naval-warfare/us-navy-contracts-alaskan-reconcraft-for-new-patrol-boats/), report, 2023-04-25.
- Trade and general reporting placed the award one day after Iran fired missiles at a third commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz, framing the timing against renewed maritime-security pressure (context only, not central to the Alaska story). [Tech Times](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320018/20260709/navy-awards-25m-stealthy-autonomous-boats-days-after-iran-breaks-hormuz-truce.htm), report, 2026-07-09.
- The award was announced in the Department's July 8, 2026 contracts list; the contract number is N00024-26-C-6324. [U.S. Department of War](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report, 2026-07-08.
- Work will be performed in Clackamas, Oregon, and is expected to be completed by November 2028. [U.S. Department of War](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report, 2026-07-08.
- The contract was not competitively procured, in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 19.805-1(b)(2), the sole-source authority under the SBA 8(a) Business Development program. [U.S. Department of War](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report, 2026-07-08.
- The award is funded from the Navy's fiscal 2026 account for accelerated procurement and fielding of innovative technologies; the full $24,960,408 was obligated at award and expires at the end of the current fiscal year. [U.S. Department of War](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report, 2026-07-08.
- ReconCraft LLC is incorporated in Alaska and headquartered in Anchorage, and holds SBA 8(a) certification and Native American / tribally-owned small-business status. [HigherGov (SAM.gov-sourced awardee profile)](https://www.highergov.com/awardee/reconcraft-llc-10114995/), report, 2026-07.
- ReconCraft's manufacturing facility is in Clackamas, Oregon; the company's own website lists its address as 9891 SE Mather Rd., Clackamas, OR 97015 and says it builds vessels up to 120 feet, 'Proudly Manufactured in the USA.'. [ReconCraft LLC (company site)](https://reconcraft.com/), report, 2026-07.
- An autonomous low-profile vessel (ALPV) is an uncrewed, semi-submersible craft whose configuration was influenced by narco-submarines; it rides low with most of the structure submerged to minimize radar, sonar, visual and infrared detection. [Army Recognition](https://armyrecognition.com/news/navy-news/2025/us-marines-train-in-japan-with-alpv-autonomous-low-profile-vessel-based-on-narco-submarine-designs-for-stealth-operations), report, 2025-04-24.
- ALPV class figures (a documented program design), about 19.75 meters (roughly 65 feet) long, less than 0.61 meters of freeboard at operating displacement, payload roughly 2,000 to 4,627 kilograms, and an operational range near 2,200 nautical miles at about 8 knots. [Army Recognition](https://armyrecognition.com/news/navy-news/2025/us-marines-train-in-japan-with-alpv-autonomous-low-profile-vessel-based-on-narco-submarine-designs-for-stealth-operations), report, 2025-04-24.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# The Interior's Power Math

> Golden Valley Electric's board weighs $120 million in new gas capacity today, and its members carry the debt.

Published 2026-07-13 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-13/

## The story

$120 million. One vote today. Members own the bill.

a co-op decides behind a closed door

A turbine, and a $120 million question

On July 13, in a closed executive session, Golden Valley Electric Association's board weighs buying a second LM6000 gas turbine for its North Pole plant. The price is about $120 million. In April the board spent $50,000 just to hold a place in the order line.

The News-Miner reports demand for these turbines has surged because large data centers need a guaranteed power supply.

One machine. Steel and megawatts.

An LM6000 makes 45 to 58 megawatts on its own, or 76 to 152 paired with steam or storage. The plant's first LM6000, from 2006, still runs at 47 megawatts. Ordering another can take three to five years.

Members just absorbed the biggest fuel hike on record.

On June 1 the fuel charge jumped 61 percent, the largest increase GVEA has ever posted. The fuel its plants burn more than doubled since February.

The loads are still on paper.

The Air Force is offering about 4,700 acres, 12 parcels across three bases, to companies that would build AI data centers. Two of them, Eielson and Clear, are in the Interior. None is built, no lease is signed. A pending defense bill would require a grid study, if it becomes law.

Firm power, soft load.

The bill is certain. The load is a maybe.

Members are being asked to finance firm, dated capacity now, while the loads that justify it stay on paper. And the vote happens in executive session, a room members reach only through board elections.

Should a co-op spend $120 million on firm power while the loads that need it are still proposals? Or wait until someone signs for the load?

## What we verified

- GVEA's board is set to weigh buying a second LM6000 turbine in an executive session on July 13. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-07.
- The North Pole plant installed a 47-megawatt naphtha-fired LM6000 in 2006 along with a 17-megawatt steam turbine. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-07.
- The LM6000 is made by General Electric. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-07.
- The Department of the Air Force is offering approximately 4,700 acres of underutilized land for potential AI data centers. [U.S. Air Force (af.mil)](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), report, 2026-04-10.
- Twelve parcels have been identified for potential data-center development across JBER, Eielson AFB and Clear Space Force Station. [U.S. Air Force (af.mil)](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), report, 2026-04-10.
- The parcels would be offered under the Enhanced Use Lease model, which leases non-excess property to partners for long-term use. [U.S. Air Force (af.mil)](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), report, 2026-04-10.
- The FY2027 NDAA provisions would require rigorous grid impact assessments before executing or renewing any Enhanced Use Lease for a data center. [Office of Sen. Dan Sullivan](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report, 2026-06.

Dan Sullivan](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report, 2026-06.
- According to Sullivan's office, the FY2027 defense bill authorizes about $2.6 billion for Alaska. [Office of Sen. Dan Sullivan](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report, 2026-06.
- The Fairbanks North Star Borough is designated a 'Serious' PM2.5 nonattainment area under the 2006 standard. [U.S. EPA Green Book](https://www3.epa.gov/airquality/greenbook/anayo_ak.html), report.
- GVEA's fuel and purchased power charge rose 7.8 cents per kilowatt hour to 20.7 cents per kilowatt hour effective June 1, 2026, an increase of 61 percent over the prior quarter. [Alaska's News Source (KTUU)](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/01/gvea-announces-rate-increase-starting-june-1-members-see-higher-bills/), report, 2026-06-01.
- A new LM6000 unit would cost about $120 million. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-07.

# First Machine to the Fire

> Five teams are racing across 1,000 square kilometers of Alaska to prove a machine can fight a wildfire with no human in the loop.

Published 2026-07-12 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-12/

## What we verified

- XPRIZE Wildfire is a four-year, $11 million global competition to accelerate solutions that end destructive wildfires. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- The finalist teams were narrowed from an original field of nearly 300 teams worldwide. [businesswire.com](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707802818/en/Dryad-Networks-Reaches-XPRIZE-Wildfire-Finals-Milestone-Demonstrating-Autonomous-Detection-and-Suppression-of-Wildfires-in-Alaska), report.
- XPRIZE Wildfire program director Andrea Santy said wildfires are becoming more frequent, intense, unpredictable and destructive. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- Dryad Networks says its Silvanet sensors and Silvaguard drone detected a small wildfire within minutes of ignition and autonomously suppressed it with no human on scene during Alaska field trials. [businesswire.com](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707802818/en/Dryad-Networks-Reaches-XPRIZE-Wildfire-Finals-Milestone-Demonstrating-Autonomous-Detection-and-Suppression-of-Wildfires-in-Alaska), report.
- Dryad says its Silvaguard drone can deliver up to 100 liters of fire suppressant directly onto an ignition point. [businesswire.com](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707802818/en/Dryad-Networks-Reaches-XPRIZE-Wildfire-Finals-Milestone-Demonstrating-Autonomous-Detection-and-Suppression-of-Wildfires-in-Alaska), report.
- Dryad says more than 30,000 Silvanet sensors have been manufactured and deployed globally and that Silvanet has been deployed by more than 50 customers worldwide. [businesswire.com](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707802818/en/Dryad-Networks-Reaches-XPRIZE-Wildfire-Finals-Milestone-Demonstrating-Autonomous-Detection-and-Suppression-of-Wildfires-in-Alaska), report.
- Dryad CEO Carsten Brinkschulte said the competition validated that ultra-early detection combined with rapid autonomous suppression can fundamentally change how society fights wildfires. [businesswire.com](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707802818/en/Dryad-Networks-Reaches-XPRIZE-Wildfire-Finals-Milestone-Demonstrating-Autonomous-Detection-and-Suppression-of-Wildfires-in-Alaska), report.
- Alaska has experienced three of its four largest fire seasons in the last 25 years. [news.asu.edu](https://news.asu.edu/20251028-science-and-technology-using-ai-help-predict-wildfires-alaska), report.
- In some years, such as 2022, Alaska accounted for nearly half of the total US acreage burned by wildfires. [news.asu.edu](https://news.asu.edu/20251028-science-and-technology-using-ai-help-predict-wildfires-alaska), report.
- ReconCraft LLC of Anchorage, Alaska was awarded a $24,960,408 firm-fixed-price contract for autonomous low-profile vessels. [war.gov](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report.
- The ReconCraft contract number is N00024-26-C-6324, a Naval Sea Systems Command award. [war.gov](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report.
- The Autonomous Wildfire Response track has five finalist teams, Anduril (USA), Data Blanket (USA), Dryad (Germany), FireSwarm Solutions (Canada), and Wildfire Quest (USA). [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- Work on the ReconCraft contract is performed in Clackamas, Oregon and is expected to be completed by November 2028. [war.gov](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report.
- The ReconCraft contract was not competitively procured, per FAR 19.805-1(b)(2). [war.gov](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report.
- The full $24,960,408 was obligated at award from FY2026 accelerated procurement and fielding of innovative technologies (Navy) funds. [war.gov](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4538357/contracts-for-july-8-2026/), report.
- According to Sen. Sullivan's office, the FY2027 NDAA authorizes a historic $2.6 billion in military construction and projects specifically for Alaska. [sullivan.senate.gov](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report.
- The FY2027 NDAA includes 56 provisions and amendments authored by Sen. Sullivan. [sullivan.senate.gov](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report.
- The bill authorizes $15 million for resilient autonomous sensing in the Arctic. [sullivan.senate.gov](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report.
- The bill authorizes $10 million for autonomy within the Golden Dome missile defense system. [sullivan.senate.gov](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report.
- The bill mandates rigorous grid impact assessments before executing or renewing any Enhanced Use Lease (EUL), reviewing energy demands and commercial grid stability. [sullivan.senate.gov](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report.
- The bill would establish an Analytics and Simulation Laboratory within the Ted Stevens Center for Arctic Security Studies. [sullivan.senate.gov](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), report.
- The Autonomous track finals field-test across a 1,000 square kilometer test zone in Alaska. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- The Alaska testing partner is the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration (ACUASI) at the University of Alaska Fairbanks Geophysical Institute. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- ACUASI is one of the FAA-designated UAS test sites. [faa.gov](https://www.faa.gov/uas/programs_partnerships/test_sites), report.
- The winning team in each XPRIZE Wildfire track receives $3.5 million. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- A $1 million bonus prize sponsored by Lockheed Martin is available to eligible Autonomous teams demonstrating superior detection. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- A $750,000 semifinal purse was distributed equally among the five Autonomous finalist teams. [xprize.org](https://www.xprize.org/news/meet-the-future-of-autonomous-wildfire-response-xprize-wildfire-announces-finalist-teams-advancing-in-11m-competition), report.
- The XPRIZE Wildfire winner is expected to be announced in September 2026. [businesswire.com](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707802818/en/Dryad-Networks-Reaches-XPRIZE-Wildfire-Finals-Milestone-Demonstrating-Autonomous-Detection-and-Suppression-of-Wildfires-in-Alaska), report.

# Cook Inlet gas storage, the RCA's no, and AI's gigawatt

> On July 10, state regulators rejected Alaska's plan to store a single winter of Cook Inlet gas.

Published 2026-07-11 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-11/

## The story

Alaska's gas machine, in cutaway.

And the valve that just shut.

Five parts move gas from rock to furnace

Reservoir trap, wellhead, pipeline, storage cavern, and the state regulator's valve. Part four is a battery for deep winter. Right now, it sits empty.

Enough for an average day. Not for January.

Cook Inlet's aging fields can meet a normal day, but not a deep-cold peak, and there is little storage to bridge the gap. A former state senator's op-ed warns of a Southcentral shortfall by 2027.

Turn a dead reservoir into a winter battery

Enstar proposed buying the depleted Kenai Loop Pool from AIX Energy and refilling it to hold 25 billion cubic feet, close to half a year's gas, for about $240 million and up to $12 a month on the average bill.

Every fix runs through one valve

The Regulatory Commission of Alaska decides whether a utility's plan is prudent before customers ever pay for it.

The regulator shut the valve

On July 10 the RCA denied the plan, calling it an "extraordinary request" that "lacked basic information about the project." The order ran 17 pages. Enstar's president said the company suspended the project.

Can it hold?

Now measure what wants to plug in

One proposed North Slope AI campus, from STAK Energy, would generate "a gigawatt or more, some 30% more than urban Alaska's peak demand." More than $10 billion at full buildout. Its comment window closes July 17.

Store one winter first?

## What we verified

- The Regulatory Commission of Alaska rejected Enstar's request for an advance determination that its gas-storage project plans were prudent, citing missing information (an 'extraordinary request' that 'lacked basic information about the project'). [Anchorage Daily News (Alex DeMarban)](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- Statewide, Alaska residential electricity rates run roughly 40% higher than the national average (former state senator's op-ed). [Anchorage Daily News (op-ed, Lesil McGuire)](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/06/opinion-alaska-needs-energy-that-works-now-and-lasts/), report, 2026-07-06.
- In many rural Alaska communities, energy costs are more than twice those in more urban parts of Alaska (op-ed). [Anchorage Daily News (op-ed, Lesil McGuire)](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/06/opinion-alaska-needs-energy-that-works-now-and-lasts/), report, 2026-07-06.
- Southcentral Alaska faces a projected Cook Inlet natural gas shortfall by 2027 (op-ed). [Anchorage Daily News (op-ed, Lesil McGuire)](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/06/opinion-alaska-needs-energy-that-works-now-and-lasts/), report, 2026-07-06.
- STAK Energy's proposed North Slope AI data-center campus generators could produce a gigawatt or more of power, some 30% more than urban Alaska's peak demand. [Northern Journal (Nathaniel Herz)](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- STAK Energy's North Slope project would cost more than $10 billion at full buildout (an earlier $500 million reference appears in the same article). [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- More than 500 public comments were received on the STAK North Slope lease before the preliminary deadline; fewer than a dozen endorsed the project. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- The STAK ADL 422741 public comment window was extended to 4:30 p.m. July 17, 2026, citing comment volume and public interest. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- The RCA order denying the plan was 17 pages long. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- Enstar's proposed Cook Inlet gas storage facility would cost $240 million. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- The project would add up to $12 a month to the average customer's bill. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- Enstar proposed buying the Kenai Loop Pool, a depleted gas reservoir, from AIX Energy for use as storage. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- The facility would initially hold 25 billion cubic feet of gas, close to half the utility's annual demand. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- The Alaska DNR has not yet completed its determination that the Kenai Loop Pool is technically capable of serving as a natural gas storage facility. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- Enstar and Hilcorp Cook Inlet have competing applications with the Alaska DNR for gas storage facility leases at the Kenai Loop Pool. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.
- Without the commission's approval, Enstar president John Sims said the company has suspended its plans to move ahead with the project. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), report, 2026-07-10.

# The Machine That Hears a Mountain Think

> Three Alaska volcanoes are on elevated alert at once, and an AI built in Fairbanks is what stands watch over them.

Published 2026-07-10 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-10/

## What we verified

- As of the July 3, 2026 AVO weekly update, Great Sitkin volcano was at Volcano Alert Level WATCH and Aviation Color Code ORANGE, with a slow lava eruption continuing in the summit crater. [volcanoes.usgs.gov](https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-AVO-2026-07-03T18:33:40+00:00), primary document, 2026-07-03.
- VOISS-Net achieves 87% classification accuracy on the test set. [jvolcanica.org](https://www.jvolcanica.org/ojs/index.php/volcanica/article/view/349), primary document, 2025-06-12.
- Alaska contains over 130 volcanoes and volcanic fields that have been active within the last two million years. [usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/avo), primary document.
- About 90 Alaska volcanoes have been active in the last 10,000 years, and more than 50 have been active in historical time (since about 1760). [usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/avo), primary document.
- Alaska's volcanoes sit under Pacific great-circle aircraft routes traversed by more than 50,000 people per day, and can erupt ash into that airspace. [usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/avo), primary document.
- As of July 3, 2026, Mount Kupreanof was at Volcano Alert Level ADVISORY and Aviation Color Code YELLOW, with seismic activity and volcanic gas emissions observed. [volcanoes.usgs.gov](https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-AVO-2026-07-03T18:33:40+00:00), primary document, 2026-07-03.
- USGS defines Volcano Alert Level WATCH as heightened/escalating unrest with increased eruption potential, or an eruption underway that poses limited hazards. [usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/VHP/volcanic-alert-levels-characterize-conditions-us-volcanoes), primary document.
- USGS defines Volcano Alert Level ADVISORY as elevated unrest above known background level, closely monitored. [usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/VHP/volcanic-alert-levels-characterize-conditions-us-volcanoes), primary document.
- Great Sitkin volcano summit elevation is 5,708 feet (1,740 m). [avo.alaska.edu](https://avo.alaska.edu/volcano/great-sitkin), primary document.
- Mount Kupreanof summit elevation is 6,217 feet (1,895 m). [avo.alaska.edu](https://avo.alaska.edu/volcano/kupreanof), primary document.
- Mount Edgecumbe summit elevation is 3,202 feet (976 m). [avo.alaska.edu](https://avo.alaska.edu/volcano/edgecumbe), primary document.
- As of July 3, 2026, Shishaldin volcano was at Volcano Alert Level ADVISORY and Aviation Color Code YELLOW, with continuing unrest. [volcanoes.usgs.gov](https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-AVO-2026-07-03T18:33:40+00:00), primary document, 2026-07-03.
- Mount Kupreanof has no real-time geophysical monitoring network and is watched primarily via satellite and regional networks. [volcanoes.usgs.gov](https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-AVO-2026-07-03T18:33:40+00:00), primary document, 2026-07-03.
- The July 3, 2026 AVO weekly update reported three Alaska volcanoes in elevated status simultaneously, Great Sitkin (Watch/Orange), Kupreanof (Advisory/Yellow), and Shishaldin (Advisory/Yellow). [volcanoes.usgs.gov](https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-AVO-2026-07-03T18:33:40+00:00), primary document, 2026-07-03.
- AVO monitors these volcanoes with a multi-sensor network including local seismic, geodetic and infrasound sensors, satellite data, web cameras, and regional infrasound and lightning networks. [volcanoes.usgs.gov](https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-AVO-2026-07-03T18:33:40+00:00), primary document, 2026-07-03.
- VOISS-Net is a generalized deep-learning (spectrogram-based CNN) model built to detect and classify volcano seismicity such as tremor, explosions, earthquakes and long-period events. [jvolcanica.org](https://www.jvolcanica.org/ojs/index.php/volcanica/article/view/349), primary document, 2025-06-12.
- VOISS-Net was trained on more than 270,000 spectrograms. [jvolcanica.org](https://www.jvolcanica.org/ojs/index.php/volcanica/article/view/349), primary document, 2025-06-12.
- VOISS-Net was developed using data from seven volcanoes across three regions, five Alaskan volcanoes, Mt. Etna in Italy, and Kilauea in Hawaii. [jvolcanica.org](https://www.jvolcanica.org/ojs/index.php/volcanica/article/view/349), primary document, 2025-06-12.
- VOISS-Net was developed collaboratively by scientists at the Alaska Volcano Observatory / University of Alaska Fairbanks and the U.S. Geological Survey. [jvolcanica.org](https://www.jvolcanica.org/ojs/index.php/volcanica/article/view/349), report, 2025-06-12.
- VolcSARvatory uses interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) to detect ground movement as small as 1 centimeter. [gi.alaska.edu](https://www.gi.alaska.edu/news/alaska-developed-volcano-monitoring-system-will-expand-across-us), report, 2025-02-20.
- The Alaska Volcano Observatory at UAF has used a prototype of VolcSARvatory since early 2022. [gi.alaska.edu](https://www.gi.alaska.edu/news/alaska-developed-volcano-monitoring-system-will-expand-across-us), report, 2025-02-20.
- VolcSARvatory's usefulness became apparent during an earthquake swarm at long-quiet Mount Edgecumbe volcano near Sitka on April 11, 2022. [gi.alaska.edu](https://www.gi.alaska.edu/news/alaska-developed-volcano-monitoring-system-will-expand-across-us), report, 2025-02-20.
- VolcSARvatory is being expanded to all USGS volcano observatories; the USGS Volcano Science Center operates AVO plus four other U.S. volcano observatories (five total). [gi.alaska.edu](https://www.gi.alaska.edu/news/alaska-developed-volcano-monitoring-system-will-expand-across-us), report, 2025-02-20.
- The UAF VolcSARvatory expansion is one of seven NASA Disasters Program proposals that share $6.3 million over two years. [gi.alaska.edu](https://www.gi.alaska.edu/news/alaska-developed-volcano-monitoring-system-will-expand-across-us), report, 2025-02-20.
- Democratic gubernatorial candidate Tom Begich argued Alaska must not fall behind on AI policy. [adn.com](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/03/opinion-what-alaskas-governor-candidates-say-about-ai-and-why-it-matters/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Gubernatorial candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins warned that the AI industry has understated public risk. [adn.com](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/03/opinion-what-alaskas-governor-candidates-say-about-ai-and-why-it-matters/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Kreiss-Tomkins emphasized Alaskan data sovereignty, saying Alaskans' data belongs to Alaskans alone. [adn.com](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/03/opinion-what-alaskas-governor-candidates-say-about-ai-and-why-it-matters/), report, 2026-07-03.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# One River, Two Ways to Count It, AI vs the Tower

> A hand-clicker on a Bristol Bay tower has counted the sockeye since 1955. This year an AI drone wants that job.

Published 2026-07-09 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-09/

## What we verified

- An autonomous drone-in-a-box launches at 8:30 a.m. on an automated flight to an observation position above the right bank of the Wood River. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Project lead Norm Van Vactor says he has been engaged in the Bristol Bay commercial fishery for 40 years. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Ian Chiu develops the machine-learning components of the project remotely. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Van Vactor calls the moment an 'amazing convergence of technology,' citing drone-in-a-box, machine learning and AI, Starlink Mini, lithium batteries and solar panels all maturing in the last year or two. [KMXT (republish of KDLG)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- The 2026 Bristol Bay preseason forecast estimates a total run of 44.05 million sockeye. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-06/bristol-bay-fisheries-report-july-6-2026), report, 2026-07-06.
- As of July 6, 2026, the total Bristol Bay sockeye run to date was 26,944,183 fish. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-06/bristol-bay-fisheries-report-july-6-2026), report, 2026-07-06.
- As of the July 6, 2026 report, Wood River tower escapement to date totaled 2,112,834 fish. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-06/bristol-bay-fisheries-report-july-6-2026), report, 2026-07-06.
- Wood River tower crews counted 57,258 sockeye on Sunday. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-06/bristol-bay-fisheries-report-july-6-2026), report, 2026-07-06.
- The Wood River escapement goal range is 700,000 to 2.8 million fish, and the 2026 run is within that range. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-06/bristol-bay-fisheries-report-july-6-2026), report, 2026-07-06.
- The story was written by Jessie Sheldon and republished statewide via KMXT on July 8, 2026 (originally KDLG, July 3, 2026). [KMXT](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- The drone imagery is fed into a computer model intended to generate more accurate salmon escapement counts. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Machine-learning developer Ian Chiu describes the end product as a computer vision model trained to pick out salmon from video. [KMXT (republish of KDLG)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- The team will likely need several thousand drone images to train the model to reliably identify a fish; technicians hand-label the imagery. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Alaska Department of Fish and Game has used counting towers for Bristol Bay escapement since 1955 (70+ years). [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Tower crews rotate through continuous 24-hour shifts, counting each passing salmon with a hand-clicker in 10-minute intervals. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Most Bristol Bay escapement counts currently come from nine Fish & Game counting tower sites. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- Project partners include the University of Washington's Fisheries Research Institute (lab at Lake Aleknagik), the Bristol Bay Regional Seafood Development Association, and the Bristol Bay Economic Development Corporation. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.
- At this stage, Alaska Department of Fish and Game is not directly involved in the drone project. [KDLG](https://www.kdlg.org/fisheries/2026-07-03/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-03.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# Alaska's AI Land Rush, Four Rooms, One Open Door

> Alaska got more than 500 public comments on a $10 billion North Slope AI data center. Fewer than a dozen said yes.

Published 2026-07-08 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-08/

## What we verified

- More than 500 public comments were submitted to Alaska DNR on the Stak Energy lease before the preliminary deadline. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Fewer than a dozen of the public comments endorsed the Stak project. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- DNR extended the ADL 422741 public comment deadline to 4:30 p.m. Alaska Daylight Time on July 17, 2026 (extension notice ID 224224). [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The original comment deadline on the Stak preliminary decision was 4:30 p.m. on June 15, 2026 (original notice ID 223817, published May 12, 2026). [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- DNR said it extended the comment period because of significant public interest, comment volume, and requests for extension. [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- DNR's Division of Oil and Gas issued a preliminary decision to offer STAK Energy Corporation a 50-year lease. [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The proposed lease covers a 715.4-acre parcel of state land. [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The parcel sits adjacent to the Dalton Highway approximately 26 miles south of Deadhorse. [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The docket is ADL 422741 with applicant STAK Energy Corporation; notice 223817 (published May 12, 2026) is the original preliminary decision notice and notice 224224 (published June 17, 2026) is the extension notice. [Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas (Online Public Notices)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- Stak's John Boyle said the full project would cost more than $10 billion. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Stak estimated approximately $500 million for initial site evaluation, engineering, gravel road and pad construction, and initial camp and support infrastructure. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Stak proposes 1 to 3 gigawatts of on-site natural gas-fired generation. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Northern Journal reports that a gigawatt of generation is some 30% more than the peak demand of urban Alaska's entire grid. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Lease documents indicate full simple-cycle operation could consume roughly 350 to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- That daily gas burn annualizes to approximately 128 to 183 billion cubic feet per year. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- The project would require roughly 7.1 million cubic yards of gravel fill. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Plans include a roughly 640-acre gravel pad. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Plans include a 1.8-mile gravel access road. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- John Boyle said most comments were form letters lacking substance. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- John Boyle is Stak's chief strategy officer and previously served as commissioner of Alaska's Department of Natural Resources from 2023 to 2025. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Opposition comments carried subject lines including 'HELL NO! To ANY DATA CENTERS' and 'NO AI'. [Copper River Country Journal (reprinting Herz)](https://www.countryjournal2020.com/2026/07/alaskans-say-no-hell-no-to-north-slope.html), report, 2026-07-06.
- One commenter urged the state to 'incorporate some AI (Alaskan intelligence) into making this decision'. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- One commenter noted their message was written 'with my own brain and fingers typing'. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Comments arrived from Kodiak, Kotzebue, Seward, Valdez, and the North Slope village of Nuiqsut. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Formal opposition or concern also came from the Northern Alaska Environmental Center, the Alaska Public Interest Research Group, and the Alaska chapter of Backcountry Hunters and Anglers. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- According to Stak, average annual temperatures at the proposed site are 12 F. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Stak expects the development to need 10% or less of the water that typical data centers use for cooling. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- After the deadline passes, DNR will assess the comments before making a final decision on the lease. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Stak said in a statement that it 'is committed to being a responsible steward of the land entrusted to us'. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- The Department of the Air Force is offering approximately 4,700 acres of underutilized land at JBER, Eielson AFB, and Clear Space Force Station for AI data centers. [U.S. Air Force (official release)](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), report, 2026-04-10.
- Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development under the program. [U.S. Air Force (official release)](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), report, 2026-04-10.
- The Air Force announced the Alaska AI data center Enhanced Use Lease opportunity on April 10, 2026. [U.S. Air Force (official release)](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), report, 2026-04-10.
- The Air Force released its Request for Lease Proposal on June 5, 2026. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/09/us-military-plans-lease-alaska-land-ai-data-centers-community-responds/), report, 2026-06-08.
- Developer lease proposals were due June 29, 2026. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/proposed-air-force-data-center-land-leases-raise-some-concerns/article_98cbed0c-6574-464a-8097-c054c46cb699.html), report, 2026-06-11.
- The RFLP identifies five potential parcels in the Eielson AFB area. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/proposed-air-force-data-center-land-leases-raise-some-concerns/article_98cbed0c-6574-464a-8097-c054c46cb699.html), report, 2026-06-11.
- Four parcels are under consideration around Clear Space Force Station, including one that would connect to the GVEA grid from the Parks Highway. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/proposed-air-force-data-center-land-leases-raise-some-concerns/article_98cbed0c-6574-464a-8097-c054c46cb699.html), report, 2026-06-11.
- One Eielson-area parcel is less than a mile from North Pole Middle School. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/proposed-air-force-data-center-land-leases-raise-some-concerns/article_98cbed0c-6574-464a-8097-c054c46cb699.html), report, 2026-06-11.
- Resident Sarah Hollister said living near data centers is described as like having a vacuum cleaner running around the clock. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/09/us-military-plans-lease-alaska-land-ai-data-centers-community-responds/), report, 2026-06-08.
- Sarah Hollister raised concern about data center heat discharge affecting permafrost. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/09/us-military-plans-lease-alaska-land-ai-data-centers-community-responds/), report, 2026-06-08.
- Hollister pointed out that three of the proposed sites would be expected to use the GVEA grid and asked whether that would affect members' bills. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/09/us-military-plans-lease-alaska-land-ai-data-centers-community-responds/), report, 2026-06-08.
- JBER commander Col. Lisa Mabbutt said Alaska is expected to receive up to $8 billion in Air Force investments over the next five years. [ExecutiveGov](https://www.executivegov.com/articles/matthew-lohmeier-air-force-visit-alaska-jber-eielson), report, 2026-06-26.
- Under Secretary of the Air Force Matthew Lohmeier toured JBER and Eielson AFB June 22 through 24, 2026. [ExecutiveGov](https://www.executivegov.com/articles/matthew-lohmeier-air-force-visit-alaska-jber-eielson), report, 2026-06-26.
- GVEA recommended that any major loads be connected to its 138-kilovolt line. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/proposed-air-force-data-center-land-leases-raise-some-concerns/article_98cbed0c-6574-464a-8097-c054c46cb699.html), report, 2026-06-11.
- The Air Force plans to choose proposals that minimize and mitigate impact and risk to the surrounding community, with utilities remaining accessible and affordable. [Air & Space Forces Magazine](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/usaf-land-ai-data-centers-three-alaska-bases/), report, 2026-04-11.
- GVEA's board will weigh whether to invest in a fuel-based generator during an executive session on July 13, 2026. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- A new LM6000 unit would cost GVEA about $120 million. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- An LM6000 can generate between 45 and 58 megawatts depending on the model. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- Costs to construct a new gas turbine power plant jumped 195% from 2019 to 2026, per a Bloomberg News report cited by the News-Miner. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- Turbine order waitlists have pushed into the early 2030s, per a Bloomberg News report cited by the News-Miner. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- Demand for the turbine units has increased due to a surge in large data centers that require a guaranteed power supply, per a Bloomberg News report. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- At its April 2026 board meeting, GVEA approved $50,000 to reserve an order spot for an LM6000 combined-cycle turbine. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/local_news/gvea-board-to-weigh-heavy-purchase-decision-in-july-as-members-raise-concerns/article_c8b5ce9d-5c3a-46bf-b261-436ea4abe02b.html), report, 2026-06-28.
- GVEA's fuel and purchased power charge rose by about 61 percent effective June 1, 2026. [KUAC](https://fm.kuac.org/energy-and-the-environment/2026-05-28/gvea-plans-extraordinarily-large-increase-in-co-op-fuel-charge), report, 2026-05-28.
- The increase costs the average residential member nearly $46 more per month. [KUAC](https://fm.kuac.org/energy-and-the-environment/2026-05-28/gvea-plans-extraordinarily-large-increase-in-co-op-fuel-charge), report, 2026-05-28.
- GVEA's power plant fuel prices roughly doubled from about $2.50 to $5.10 per gallon. [KUAC](https://fm.kuac.org/energy-and-the-environment/2026-05-28/gvea-plans-extraordinarily-large-increase-in-co-op-fuel-charge), report, 2026-05-28.
- House-Senate conference committee members unveiled a draft compromise AKLNG tax bill on Thursday, July 2, 2026. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- The draft compromise would replace the state's property tax with a volumetric tax on gas after five years of operation or once flow reaches 500 million cubic feet per day, whichever comes first. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- The draft extends the construction completion deadline for the gas line and phase one from 2032 to December 31, 2034. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- Phase one of the project is an 807-mile gas line from the North Slope to Cook Inlet. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- Glenfarne owns 75% of the Alaska LNG project. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- Lawmakers are tentatively planning House and Senate floor votes on the compromise bill for Thursday, July 16, 2026. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- Lawmakers are in a second special session called by Gov. Mike Dunleavy, scheduled to end July 19, 2026. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- Dunleavy has called the corporate income tax provision a 'poison pill' and pledged to veto any bill that includes it. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- The governor and the developer have said the S corp tax in the draft will hurt the project's ability to secure financing. [Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-06/alaska-lawmakers-roll-out-draft-compromise-tax-cut-bill-for-the-proposed-aklng-gas-line), report, 2026-07-06.
- On the Wood River, an automated drone emerges from its box at exactly 8:30 a.m. and takes off on an automated flight path. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- The team expects to need several thousand drone images for the computer-vision model to learn to reliably identify a fish. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- Alaska Fish and Game has been tracking salmon escapement since 1955. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- Tower technicians count each passing salmon with a hand-clicker in 10-minute intervals. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- Tower crews rotate through continuous shifts over 24 hours. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- Most escapement counts across Bristol Bay currently come from nine Fish and Game counting tower sites. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- The pilot is run with the University of Washington's Fisheries Research Institute, the Bristol Bay Regional Seafood Development Association, and the Bristol Bay Economic Development Corporation. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- Norm Van Vactor is a project lead on the drone counting pilot. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- In the project's next phase, the crew will test their models against Fish and Game tower counting data. [Alaska Public Media / KDLG](https://alaskapublic.org/news/environment/2026-07-08/ai-drones-and-salmon-what-new-technology-could-mean-for-bristol-bay-sockeye-counts), report, 2026-07-08.
- BBRSDA's drone salmon-monitoring project received a $70,000 Seafood Industry Climate Award grant from the Acme Smoked Fish Foundation. [Acme Smoked Fish Foundation (funder)](https://acmesmokedfish.com/pages/seafood-and-climate-initiatives), report, 2026-01-26.
- According to the funder, the drone project enables managers to detect salmon run timing up to 24 hours earlier. [Acme Smoked Fish Foundation (funder)](https://acmesmokedfish.com/pages/seafood-and-climate-initiatives), report, 2026-01-26.
- The 2026 preseason forecast expects a Bristol Bay total run of 44.05 million sockeye. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-02/fish-numbers-july-2-2026), report, 2026-07-02.
- The Bristol Bay run had reached 17,011,218 sockeye through July 1, 2026, as reported July 2. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-02/fish-numbers-july-2-2026), report, 2026-07-02.
- Wood River tower crews counted 123,489 sockeye on Wednesday, July 1, bringing their cumulative count to 1,884,747 fish. [KDLG Bristol Bay Fisheries Report](https://www.kdlg.org/show/bristol-bay-fisheries-report/2026-07-02/fish-numbers-july-2-2026), report, 2026-07-02.
- Alaska's 2026 primary election is August 18, 2026. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Alaska_gubernatorial_election), report.
- Incumbent Gov. Mike Dunleavy is term-limited and ineligible to seek a third consecutive term. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Alaska_gubernatorial_election), report.
- Alaska saw over 9,000 lightning strikes in a single day in late June 2026, amid a week of prolific lightning. [Alaska Wildland Fire Information (interagency)](https://akfireinfo.com/2026/06/26/air-resources-assist-with-several-new-lightning-fires-managed-by-u-s-wildland-fire-service/), report, 2026-06-26.
- A U.S. Forest Service Uncrewed Aircraft System module from Boise, Idaho was assigned to fly reconnaissance, mapping, and infrared missions on the Polly Fire. [Alaska Wildland Fire Information (interagency)](https://akfireinfo.com/2026/06/26/air-resources-assist-with-several-new-lightning-fires-managed-by-u-s-wildland-fire-service/), report, 2026-06-26.
- The Cecil Fire is approximately 724 acres and 100% contained, with 18 personnel assigned, as of July 6, 2026. [Alaska Wildland Fire Information (interagency)](https://akfireinfo.com/2026/07/06/cecil-fire-reaches-full-containment-big-fire-at-70-as-work-nears-end/), report, 2026-07-06.
- A UAS drone flight on July 6, 2026 detected no remaining heat on the Cecil Fire. [Alaska Wildland Fire Information (interagency)](https://akfireinfo.com/2026/07/06/cecil-fire-reaches-full-containment-big-fire-at-70-as-work-nears-end/), report, 2026-07-06.
- A permafrost digital twin under a Utqiagvik road embankment was built from a pair of one-kilometer fiber-optic cables that collected temperature and seismic data from September 2021 to June 2024. [Penn State University (news release)](https://www.psu.edu/news/research/story/digital-twins-could-help-melt-mystery-alaskas-thawing-permafrost), report, 2026-06-16.
- The digital twin approach more accurately predicted the embankment permafrost's unfrozen water content, ground temperature changes, and heat movement. [Penn State University (news release)](https://www.psu.edu/news/research/story/digital-twins-could-help-melt-mystery-alaskas-thawing-permafrost), report, 2026-06-16.
